images.after: Build your first automation, step by step
images.title: Your first form-to-spreadsheet automation
images.alt: Steps to build a no-code automation: do it by hand, choose the trigger, add the action, map fields, test with real data, turn it on and check history.
images.caption: Slow down on field mapping: a wrong mapping still runs without an error.

items.title: Do it by hand once
items.text: Note which form field goes in which spreadsheet column.

items.title: Choose the trigger
items.text: Pick your form app and the "new submission" event, then connect accounts.

items.title: Add the action
items.text: Choose "add row" and the exact file and sheet, with a header row in place.

items.title: Map the fields
items.text: Name to Name, email to Email, message to Message.

items.title: Test with real data
items.text: Use a long message and an accented name, then check every column.

items.title: Turn it on and check
items.text: Switch it on, submit once more, and find that run in the history.

images.title: How Zapier and Make count usage
images.alt: Comparison of Zapier and Make: Zapier counts successful action steps as tasks, Make charges a credit for every module including the trigger.
images.caption: The free allowances aren't comparable at face value, so count what a run actually uses.

columns.label: Zapier
points: Free plan: one trigger, one action

columns.label: Make
points: A credit each time a module acts
The trigger uses a credit too
Visual canvas takes longer to learn
Free plan lets you chain several steps

images.after: What goes wrong, and how to limit it
images.title: Keep automations from failing quietly
images.alt: Checklist for safer automations: failure notifications, monthly run history checks, comparing counts, minimal data, and drafts for customer emails.
images.caption: Nothing announces a broken automation unless you set it up to.

items: Turn on failure notifications in your tool
Open the run history once a month
Compare counts: form submissions against sheet rows
Don't automate a process you haven't settled
Send only the fields you need, nothing sensitive
Mention the services you use in your privacy policy
Have customer-facing emails create drafts until you trust them
